name: Cylinder Heads
description: Gen V LT cylinder heads, valves, springs/retainers/locks, seals, MLS head gaskets and the head fasteners with full torque sequences (GM TTY and ARP stud/bolt options).

components.name: Cylinder heads (pair)
components.description: Aluminum reverse-cooled Gen V heads with 2 valves per cylinder, rectangular intake ports, flat-oval exhaust ports, and the direct injector bored into the chamber between the valves. LT4 heads are rotocast A356-T6 with 65.47 cc chambers, titanium intake valves and sodium-filled exhaust valves; LT1 heads are 319-T7 with 59.02 cc chambers.
components.location: On each bank deck, tilted 45° outboard; left (driver) head carries cylinders 1-3-5-7, right head 2-4-6-8.

factory.name: GM LT4 cylinder head (rotocast A356-T6)
factory.notes: Casting 12646956; 65.47 cc chamber; intake valve 2.126 in titanium, exhaust 1.590 in sodium-filled; valve angles 12.5° int / 12.0° exh. LT1 heads: 12678633 / 12620544 / 12620545 (casting 12620549), 59.02 cc, 297 cc intake runner, 107 cc exhaust runner.

raceOptions.name: Edelbrock Victor Jr. Gen V LT1 race head
raceOptions.notes: Exhaust ports raised/moved 1.5 in horizontally - custom headers required. Check intake bolt pattern vs supercharger.

raceOptions.name: CNC-ported factory LT4/LT1 castings (SDPC Raceshop, BTR, Katech, etc.)
raceOptions.notes: Retains factory DI injector bores, manifold and header fitment - most practical for a road-race car.

installNotes: Clean deck surfaces (no abrasive pads on MLS sealing surfaces); check head flatness.
Fit head gasket over dowels, lower head straight down onto dowels.
CC chambers and check valve-job concentricity when using ported heads.
inspection: Leak-down test; look for coolant in cylinders; check for exhaust-side cracking between seats at rebuild.

components.name: Cylinder head gaskets (MLS)
components.description: Multi-layer steel head gaskets sealing combustion, coolant and oil between deck and head. Bore size and compressed thickness change compression ratio and quench; boosted race engines use a stout MLS gasket, often with studs.
components.location: Between each block deck and cylinder head.

factory.name: GM Gen V 6.2L MLS head gasket
factory.notes: Listed in the Michigan Motorsports LT4 AFM delete kit as the Gen V 6.2L MLS head gasket pair.

installNotes: Install clean and dry, no sealant, "this side up/front" marks per gasket.
inspection: Compression/leak-down; coolant level/pressure trends; combustion gas test of coolant if overheating.

components.name: Cylinder head bolts / studs
components.description: Each head is clamped by 10 M12 x 1.75 fasteners (factory torque-to-yield bolts, one short Allen-head bolt at the front of the left head) plus M8 corner fasteners on blocks that are drilled for them. Race builds use ARP head studs; ARP warns some blocks need machining to accept the M8 studs.
components.location: Through each cylinder head into the block deck.

factory.name: GM TTY head bolts: (10) M12 x 1.75 per head + M8 corner bolts
factory.notes: Summit lists M12 x 1.75 x 134.0 (standard) and M12 x 1.75 x 102.0 (1 bolt, LH side). Factory threads have locking compound - chase before reassembly.

hardware.item: GM head bolt M12 x 1.75 x 134 (standard, 19 per engine)
hardware.torqueSequence: GM/ARP 10-bolt (M12) sequence per head, viewed from the outside: 1 = center upper, 2 = center lower, 3 = upper rear-of-center, 4 = lower rear-of-center, 5 = upper front-of-center, 6 = lower front-of-center, 7 = upper rearmost, 8 = lower rearmost, 9 = upper frontmost (short bolt/stud location, driver side only), 10 = lower frontmost. M8 corner fasteners last. Pass 1: all 10 to 59 ft-lb in sequence. Pass 2: +90° in sequence. Pass 3: +60° (standard bolts).
hardware.threadlocker: Clean engine oil on threads/under head (new bolts)
hardware.notes: Summit (LT1 and LT4 tables) and Michigan Motorsports agree: 59 ft-lb, +90°, +60°.

hardware.item: GM short Allen-head bolt M12 x 1.75 x 102 (LH head, forwardmost, 1 per engine)
hardware.spec: M12 x 1.75 x 102.0 mm TTY Allen head
hardware.torqueSequence: Position 9 on the left head: 59 ft-lb, +90°, final +40°.
hardware.notes: Left head only (qty 1 per engine; 0 on right head).

hardware.spec: M8 x 1.25 (count per head varies by block; verify)
hardware.notes: Value not found in public Gen V sources; 22 ft-lb is the Gen III/IV M8 head-bolt value. Confirm with GM service information. Checked 2026-10: the GM SI fastener table for the C7 LT1 (screenshots reposted on CorvetteForum) lists only M12 head bolts (standard +90°/+60°, internal-hex +90°/+40°, and a 'short bolts' group with a +55° final pass). No GM M8 head-bolt value was found. If your block uses M8 corner fasteners, they normally come in the ARP kit; use the ARP sheet value. Downgraded from typical to estimate.

hardware.item: ARP 234-4343 M12 head stud nut (12-pt) with washer
hardware.torque: 40 ft-lb (54 N·m), then 80 ft-lb (108 N·m), then 115 ft-lb (156 N·m)
hardware.torqueSequence: GM/ARP 10-bolt (M12) sequence per head, viewed from the outside: 1 = center upper, 2 = center lower, 3 = upper rear-of-center, 4 = lower rear-of-center, 5 = upper front-of-center, 6 = lower front-of-center, 7 = upper rearmost, 8 = lower rearmost, 9 = upper frontmost (short bolt/stud location, driver side only), 10 = lower frontmost. M8 corner fasteners last. Three passes 40/80/115 ft-lb on nuts 1-10.
hardware.threadlocker: ARP Ultra-Torque on stud threads and nut face; washers and head spot-faces DRY
hardware.notes: Studs installed hand tight only - hex broach is for install, not torque.

hardware.item: ARP 234-4347 M12 head stud nut (Custom Age 625+)
hardware.torque: 50 ft-lb (68 N·m), then 100 ft-lb (136 N·m), then 150 ft-lb (203 N·m)
hardware.torqueSequence: GM/ARP 10-bolt (M12) sequence per head, viewed from the outside: 1 = center upper, 2 = center lower, 3 = upper rear-of-center, 4 = lower rear-of-center, 5 = upper front-of-center, 6 = lower front-of-center, 7 = upper rearmost, 8 = lower rearmost, 9 = upper frontmost (short bolt/stud location, driver side only), 10 = lower frontmost. M8 corner fasteners last. Washer stamped side down against head.
Step 4 - after all M12 nuts are at final torque.

installNotes: Chase all block threads (ARP 912-0008 or 912-0016 for M12x1.75, 912-0001 for M8x1.25) and blow out holes - factory thread compound will stop new fasteners short.
Clean head spot faces with solvent; keep washer faces dry (ARP).
Torque in sequence in the passes listed in hardware; M8 corner fasteners last.
ARP note: some blocks are pre-drilled for M8 studs, others need machining.
inspection: Re-torque is NOT applicable to GM TTY bolts; with ARP studs follow ARP guidance (generally no re-torque on MLS).

components.name: Valve springs, retainers & locks
components.description: Factory LT springs are beehive single springs; any cam with more lift/rpm (or a road-race rev limit above stock) needs a dual-spring kit with titanium or tool-steel retainers. Locks (keepers) must match retainer angle.
components.location: On each valve stem, top of the head under the rocker arms.

factory.name: GM beehive valve spring (natural color), steel retainer, locks

raceOptions.name: BTR SK007 dual .660 in lift spring kit (titanium retainers, seals, locks)
raceOptions.notes: Specified with BTR Gen V 220 cam.

raceOptions.name: PAC / COMP / Manton dual spring kits for Gen V
raceOptions.notes: Choose for cam lift and target rpm; check coil bind margin and retainer-to-seal clearance.

installNotes: Measure installed height per valve and shim to spec.
Check seat/open pressure on a spring tester.
Seat locks with a light mallet tap on the retainer (with a socket) after assembly.
inspection: Check seat pressure every few events on an endurance engine; look for broken spring fragments in the oil filter.
